### Experimental model and participant details

Cell lines were originally obtained from the ATCC bioresource or from collaborators where noted. Cells were maintained in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle medium (DMEM) with high glucose (Thermo Fisher #11965) supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (FBS), l-glutamine (1%), 1% essential amino acids, 1% sodium pyruvate and 1% penicillin–streptomycin and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO2. For the lymphocyte experiments from the patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, cells were grown in suspension in RPMI 1640, 2 mM l-glutamine, 15% FBS and 1% penicillin–streptomycin. Informed consent was obtained from all participants and/or their legal guardians. They provide written consent for their Epstein–Bar virus immortalized cell lines and DNA to be used for research purposes. The study was approved by the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia under IRB protocol 07–005352. All experiments were performed in accordance with the relevant IRB guidelines and regulations.

### ChromORFeome library transduction

U2OS cells were plated in 384-well plates (350 cells per well). The following day, cells were spin-infected with the lentivirus-packaged chromORFeome library (1 μl of virus per well) in the presence of 4 μg ml−1 polybrene. Twenty-four hours later, blasticidin was added to cells to a final concentration of 15 μg ml−1. Experiments were performed after 5 days of selection with blasticidin.

### High-throughput UV-laser microirradiation

U2OS cells were infected 384-well plates (Greiner Bio-One #781090) with the chromORFeome library as described in this section. After a 5-day selection period with blasticidin, cells reached 90% confluence. Cells were presensitized with Hoechst 33258 (Sigma-Aldrich B2883) (10 μg ml−1) for 20 min before laser microirradiation. Hoescht incubation and microirradiation experiments were conducted in DMEM without phenol red and supplemented with penicillin–streptomycin and 10% FBS. A Palm microdissector with Robosoftware (v3.2) was used to induce DNA breaks with a 355-nm solid-state laser (UV-A) in a high-throughput manner across the 384-well plate. First, cells were focused with the 20× objective. Then, under the 2.5× objective, a line was ‘drawn’ across the middle of all the wells in the first row by using the ‘Element’ tool in the Palm Robosoftware menu. Copy and paste of the line element was performed in all the rows of the plate by using the Palm Robosoftware menu. The 20× objective was used to refocus the cells and perform the laser irradiation as the following: all the line elements created in all rows were selected at a time, or one by one, then the tool ‘start cutting laser’ was selected to initiate the microirradiation. The microdissector generated a UV-laser path across all the wells in the first row of the 384-well plate and continued irradiating consecutive rows in an automated manner, while the focus was adjusted manually during the process. The microdissector took 7 min to irradiate a row. The library was split in four 384-well plates that were irradiated consecutively. The conditions used for the laser microbeam were the following: speed 100%, focus 72 and energy 50%. Twenty minutes after microirradiation, cells were washed with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 10 min, and immunostaining was performed as previously described in this section using the primary antibodies anti-phospho-H2AX (Ser139) (Cell Signaling #9718) 1:1,000 and anti-V5 tag (Abcam #27671) 1:500 overnight at 4 °C. After secondary antibody incubation, cells were kept in PBS until imaging. Immunostaining was assessed using a Leica DMI4000 B immunofluorescence microscope. The path of DNA breaks across the nuclei in the plate was detected by the presence of a positive staining of γH2AX stripes in nuclei. In those nuclei with positive staining of γH2AX, the presence of a stripe colocalizing with γH2AX stripe was assessed in the V5 channel. A positive V5 stripe colocalizing with γH2AX in a well would suggest the recruitment of the candidate protein to DNA breaks (or chromatin surrounding a DNA break), while an anti-stripe pattern would suggest the candidate protein moving out from damaged chromatin. Representative images of V5-striped or anti-striped nuclei were acquired using the 40× objective.

### Plasmids, lentiviral production and infection, and transfection with siRNA

Lentivirus were generated by transfecting 293T cells with 6 μg of the indicated vectors (pLX304 or pLKO) and the packaging plasmids pMDG2 (1.5 μg) and psPAX (3.5 μg) using polyethylenimine reagent (33 μl from 1 mg ml−1 stock) in 500 μl of Opti-MEM medium. Plasmid containing Opti-MEM medium was added to a 10-cm tissue culture plate containing approximately 2 × 106 293T cells in 6 ml of complete DMEM medium. The 293T medium was changed 24 h after transfection, with 6 ml of fresh complete DMEM added to a 10-cm tissue culture plate. Virus-containing supernatants were collected 48 h after transfection and passed through a 0.45-μm filter. Cells were infected with an equal ratio of supernatant containing viral particles to cell culture medium and 8 μg ml−1 polybrene in a 6-well plate, for 8 h at 37 °C. Cells were selected with blasticidin-containing (pLX304) or puromycin-containing (pLKO) medium 48 h after infection. Lentivirus of pLX304 from the human ORFeome56 was produced to generate U2OS cell lines overexpressing candidate hits for validation experiments including ZNF280A overexpression. Lentivirus of pLKO was used to knock down human ZNF280A in U2OS and HeLa cells.

siRNA transfections (30–90 nM per transfection) were carried out using Lipofectamine RNAi Max (Invitrogen #13778030) according to the manufacturer’s instructions, with total siRNA not exceeding 90 nM. siRNA cocktail in Opti-MEM was added to 6 ml of fresh DMEM and removed after 8 h, followed by replenishment with complete DMEM. All experiments were performed at least 48 h after knockdown. Assessment of siRNA knockdown by immunoblotting or real-time PCR (RT-PCR) was performed 72 h after transfection.

### Immunofluorescence

Cells were plated on poly-d-lysine-coated coverslips (50 μg ml−1) (Sigma-Aldrich) 24 h before treatment with ionizing radiation (3 Gy) or camptothecin (1 μM). For BrdU labelling studies, after siRNA transfection, cells were pretreated with 30 μM BrdU for 36 h before a 4-h treatment with 1 μM camptothecin. Coverslips were placed into ice-cold preextraction buffer for 7 min (10 mM PIPES pH 6.8, 300 mM sucrose, 20 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl2 and 0.5% Triton X-100), then fixed for 10 min in 4% PFA. After washing in PBS and 1 h block (10% fetal calf serum in PBS), cells were incubated in primary antibody overnight at 4 °C and secondary antibody at 1:250 for 1 h at room temperature. Cells were washed three times with PBS and mounted onto glass slides with Prolong gold anti-fade reagent with DAPI (Life Technologies). Images were acquired using a Nikon Eclipse Ti inverted microscope using 60× magnification (unless stated) and the Nikon Nis Elements software v4.6. ImageJ was used to overlay images acquired from different fluorescent channels. Colocalization was classified as when the image overlay was at least 50% between foci acquired on each fluorescent channel. Each experiment was performed with at least three independent biological repeats. The number of nuclei analysed for each experiment is noted in the figure legends.

### UV-laser microirradiation

U2OS stable cell lines generated by infection with candidate ORFs were seeded in 8-well glass surface chamber slides (Lab-Tek II, Nunc #154534) at a density of 50,000–80,000 cells per well to have cells at 80% confluency at the time of microirradiation. The following day, cells were presensitized with the nucleotide analogue BrdU (Sigma-Aldrich #B5002) 10 μM for 24 h, or alternatively, with the DNA-intercalating dye Hoechst 33258 (Sigma-Aldrich #B2883) 10 μg ml−1 for 20 min before laser microirradiation. During presensitization and microirradiation steps, cells were kept in DMEM without phenol red supplemented with penicillin–streptomycin and 10% FBS.

The MMI CellCut system (Molecular Machines & Industries) included a 355-nm solid-state laser at 4 mW and 56% power using a 40× magnification lens (0.6 aperture). After a recovery time of 20 min, cells were subjected to immunostaining as described above. The following primary antibodies and dilutions were used: anti-V5 tag (Abcam #ab27671) 1:1,000; anti-phospho-H2AX (Ser139) (Cell Signaling #9718). Images were captured in a fluorescence microscope under 20× or 40× magnification and manually analysed for the detection of V5-positive stripes or anti-stripes at DNA breaks, through colocalization with γH2AX or PAR stripes.

### Live cell imaging

For laser microirradiation, cells were plated in 3.5-cm glass-bottom dishes (MatTek, P35GC-1.5–14-C) in DMEM with 10% FBS. Twenty-four hours after seeding, 1 μg of GFP-tagged ZNF208A or empty vector was transfected into cells using Lipofectamine 2000 according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Forty-eight hours after transfection, the live cells were irradiated with 405-nm laser light. Cells were kept on a 37 °C thermos plate in normal medium during observation. The laser beam passed through a PLAON 69× oil lens to induce damage. The images were captured at each indicated timeline after damage induction (0 min, 5 min, 10 min, 15 min, 20 min, 30 min, 45 min and 60 min). For the evaluation of the accumulation and kinetics, ImageJ was used to measure the mean intensity of each accumulated point or line obtained after subtraction of the background intensity in the irradiated cells.

### Immunoblotting

Cells were rinsed once with cold PBS and lysed in ice-cold RIPA buffer containing 50 mM Tris–HCl (pH 7.5), 150 mM NaCl, 1% IgePal, 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), 5 mM EDTA, protease inhibitor cocktail (Complete Mini, Roche Diagnostics), 2 μM sodium orthovanadate (Na3VO4), 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), 5 μM trichostatin A (TSA) and 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF). Cell lysates were incubated on ice for 20 min, sonicated and clarified by centrifugation at 16,000g for 10 min at 4 °C. Protein concentration was quantified using Protein Assay Dye Reagent Concentrate (Bio-Rad #5000006).

Equal amounts of protein were denatured with Laemmli buffer, boiled for 5 min and loaded into Tris-glycine precast gels (4–20% Mini-PROTEAN TGX precast protein gels from Bio-Rad), resolved by SDS polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and analysed by immunoblotting. Western blot analysis was performed according to standard procedures onto polyvinylidene difluoride membrane (EMD Millipore). Transferred proteins were blocked with 5% non-fat milk powder in PBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (Sigma-Aldrich) for 1 h at room temperature and incubated with the corresponding antibodies in tris-buffered saline with 0.1% Tween-20 with 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) overnight at 4 °C. Horseradish-peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibodies were used (1 h at room temperature) for immunodetection.

### Co-immunoprecipitation

Sonicated whole-cell lysates were subjected to immunoprecipitation using magnetic Dynabeads Protein-A (Invitrogen, 10006D) or Protein-G (Invitrogen, 10007D) immunoprecipitation kits. Before immunoprecipitation, magnetic beads were conjugated with specific primary antibodies (see list of antibodies) for 6–8 h at 4 °C with constant rotation. Samples were incubated at 4 °C with constant rotation overnight in immunoprecipitation buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 5 mM NaF, 1 mM DTT, 0.05% Triton X-100, 5% glycerol, 0.25 mM PMSF plus protease inhibitors cocktail tablets (Sigma-Aldrich, 4693116001)). Magnetic dynabeads containing immunoprecipitated samples were then washed three times with immunoprecipitation buffer, before denaturing using Laemmli buffer, by boiling for 10 min at 95 °C. Clean-blot HRP-IP detection reagent (Thermo Fisher #21230) was used to limit detection of IgG heavy and light chain in immunoprecipitation immunoblot analysis.

### Clonogenic survival assays

Cells were plated in triplicate at low density 24 h before treatment with increasing doses of ionizing radiation, etoposide (Selleck Chemicals), camptothecin (Sigma) or olaparib (AZD2281, Selleck Chemicals). Cell densities were adjusted in accordance with increasing dose of DNA damaging agent. Cells were treated with camptothecin (4 h) or etoposide (6 h) before being washed once in PBS, followed by supplementation with fresh complete DMEM. For olaparib treatment, complete DMEM containing fresh drug was supplemented to cells every 3 days. Colonies were fixed and stained after 10–14 days with 2% methylene blue (Sigma-Aldrich) in 50% ethanol. Plates were manually counted, and colonies with more than 50 cells were scored. Relative survival data are normalized to respective non-treatment control (set at 100%).

### Metaphase spread analysis

Chromosomal aberrations were scored in Giemsa-stained metaphase spreads. For chromosome aberrations, demecolcine (Sigma) was added 3–4 h before collection at a final concentration of 0.2 μg ml−1. Cells were collected by trypsinization, subjected to hypotonic shock for 1 h at 37 °C in 0.3 M sodium citrate and fixed in 3:1 methanol:acetic acid solution. Cells were dropped onto acetic-acid-humidified slides, stained for 15 min in Giemsa-modified (Sigma) solution (5% v/v in H2O) and washed in water for 5 min.

### U2OS DR–GFP reporter assay

U2OS DR–GFP cells were seeded in triplicate in 12-well plates at a density of 30,000 cells per well. siRNA transfections (45 nM) were carried out using Lipofectamine RNAi Max, as described above. Twenty-four hours later, cells were transfected with 0.4 μg of I-SceI per well, using LipoD293 transfection reagent. DNA transfection cocktail was left on for 6 h, followed by medium replenishment. Forty-eight hours after I-SceI transfection, cells were trypsinized and the percentage of GFP-positive cells was determined by flow cytometry (FlowJo Software).

### U2OS–Fok1 DSB reporter assay

U2OS ER–mCherry–Lak1–Fok1 cells were plated on poly-d-lysine-coated coverslips (50 μg ml−1) (Sigma-Aldrich) 24 h before treatment with 10 μM of 4-OHT and 0.5 μM Shield-1 ligand for either 2 or 4 h, to induce DNA DSBs. Coverslips were placed into ice-cold preextraction buffer for 7 min (10 mM PIPES pH 6.8, 300 mM sucrose, 20 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl2 and 0.5% Triton X-100), then fixed for 10 min in 4% PFA. IF staining was performed as described above. Staining for 53BP1 was performed to locate DNA DSB sites.

### AsiSI real-time PCR DNA resection assay

U2OS AsiSi cells were transfected with 45 nM siRNA as described above. Forty-eight hours after transfection, cells were treated with 300 nM 4-OHT for 4 h in DMEM, 10% FBS, penicillin/streptomycin, to induce DNA DSBs. Cells were washed twice with PBS and collected in 1 ml of PBS using a cell scraper. Cells were pelleted by centrifugation, and DNA was extracted using DNAeasy kit as per the manufacturer’s instructions (Qiagen), followed by elution in 50 μl of nuclease-free water. Extracted genomic DNA was treated with 5 units RNAse H for 15 min at 37 °C. Five microlitres of DNA (approximately 0.5–1 μg DNA) was used for each condition (BsrG1 digestion and matched undigested sample). DNA digests were carried out in 30 μl, with 20 units of BsrG1 enzyme in CUTSMART digestion buffer (NEB), at 37 °C overnight. BsrG1 enzyme was heat-inactivated according to the manufacturer’s instructions (80 °C for 20 min). Twenty microlitres of nuclease-free water was added to each sample, and 2 μl of sample was used directly for RT-PCR. The percentage of ssDNA (ssDNA%) generated by resection at selected sites was determined as previously described40. In brief, for each sample, a ΔCt was calculated by subtracting the Ct value of the mock-digested sample from the Ct value of the digested sample. The undigested sample serves as a loading control for genomic DNA for each experimental condition. The ssDNA% was calculated with the following equation: s s D N A % = 1 / ( 2 ( Δ C t − 1 ) + 0.5 ) × 100 .

### Expression and purification of recombinant proteins

BLM was expressed in Spodoptera frugiperda 9 insect cells using a bac-to-bac baculovirus expression system and purified by first binding to amylose resin followed by the cleavage of MBP tag with prescission protease and subsequently binding to nickel-NTA agarose resin followed by dialysis for 2 h. Human RPA was expressed in Escherichia coli and purified using ÄKTA pure (GE Healthcare) with HiTrap Blue HP, HiTrap desalting and HiTrap Q chromatography columns (all GE Healthcare)57. DNA2 was expressed in Spodoptera frugiperda 9 insect cells and purified by affinity chromatography exploiting the N-terminal 6×His tag and the C-terminal flag tag25,57.

### DNA substrate preparation

The Y-structured DNA substrate was prepared by annealing of the oligonucleotides PC1253 and PC1254. Oligonucleotides used in this study are listed in Supplementary Table 1. Oligonucleotide-based DNA substrates were radiolabeled at the 3′ terminus with [α-32P] dCTP (PerkinElmer) and terminal transferase (New England Biolabs) according to the manufacturer’s instructions25. Unincorporated nucleotides were removed using Micro Bio-Spin P-30 Tris chromatography columns (Bio-Rad). The 2.2-kbp-long dsDNA was prepared as published before29 by amplifying the human NBS1 gene, where, during PCR, in addition to cold dNTPs, radioactive [α-32P]-dCTP was added to make it randomly labelled.

### DNA unwinding assays

DNA unwinding assays (15 μl volume) were carried out in a reaction buffer containing 25 mM Tris–acetate (pH 7.5 at 25 °C), 5 mM magnesium acetate, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 mg ml−1 BSA, 1 mM phosphoenolpyruvate, 80 U ml−1 pyruvate kinase, 100 or 150 mM NaCl as indicated, 1 mM ATP and 0.1 nM 32P-labelled oligonucleotide-based DNA substrate (in molecules). The reaction was assembled on ice, initiated by the addition of ATP and incubated at 37 °C for 30 min. Next, 5 μl of 2% STOP solution (150 mM EDTA, 2% SDS, 30% glycerol and 0.1% bromophenol blue) and 1 μl of proteinase K (20.3 mg ml−1, Roche) was added to stop the reaction for 10 min at 37 °C. To avoid reannealing of the unwound products, the 2% STOP solution was supplemented with 20-fold molar excess of the cold oligonucleotide that is 32P-labelled in the DNA substrate. The products were separated on 10% native polyacrylamide gel, and gels were transferred on 17 CHR chromatography paper (Whatman), dried, exposed to storage phosphor screens (GE Healthcare) and scanned by Typhoon FLA 9500 (GE Healthcare).

### DNA-end resection assays

DNA-end resection assays with PCR-based dsDNA substrate were performed in 15 μl volume in a reaction buffer containing 25 mM Tris–acetate (pH 7.5 at 25 °C), 2 mM magnesium acetate, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 mg ml−1 BSA, 1 mM phosphoenolpyruvate, 80 U ml−1 pyruvate kinase, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM ATP and 1 nM 32P-labelled PCR-based DNA substrate (in molecules). The reaction was assembled on ice and incubated at 37 °C for 15 min. Next, 5 μl of 2% STOP solution (150 mM EDTA, 2% SDS, 30% glycerol and 0.1% bromophenol blue) and 1 μl of proteinase K (20.3 mg ml−1, Roche) were added to stop the reaction for 10 min at 37 °C. Samples were analysed by 1% agarose gel electrophoresis, dried on DE81 chromatography paper (Whatman), exposed to storage phosphor screens (GE Healthcare) and scanned by Typhoon FLA 9500 (GE Healthcare).

### Chromatin extraction

Cells were collected in ice-cold PBS using a cell scraper and pelleted using centrifugation. The cell pellet was resuspended on ice for 20 min in 2–5 volumes of cell lysis buffer (10 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 10 mM KCl and 0.05% NP-40), supplemented with fresh protease inhibitor cocktail (Complete Mini, Roche Diagnostics), 2 μM sodium orthovanadate (Na3VO4), 1 mM DTT, 5 μM trichostatin A and 1 mM PMSF. Samples were than centrifuged at 15,000g at 4 °C for 10 min, and the supernatant containing the cytoplasmic fraction removed. A second centrifugation at 15,000g at 4 °C for 10 min was performed to ensure clean fractions. The remaining supernatant was removed, and the pellet resuspended with 2–5 volumes of HCl (0.2 N) on ice for 20 min, followed by centrifugation at 15,000g at 4 °C for 10 min. The supernatant containing acid-soluble proteins (for example, histones) was removed and neutralized with the same volume of 1 M Tris–HCl pH 8.

### Electromobility shift assay

Increasing concentrations of HA-ZNF280A (Creative Biomart; #ZNF280A 346H) were incubated with 5′-end fluorophore-labelled ssDNA or dsDNA in buffer (35 mM Tris–HCl (pH 7.5), 1 mM DTT, 10 mM EDTA, 50 μg ml−1 BSA and 50 mM KCl) at 37 °C for 15 min. RNA extraction was performed using RNeasy kit (#74106) per the manufacturer’s instructions (Qiagen). cDNA synthesis was performed with 500 ng total RNA and random hexamers using a SuperScript IV First-Strand cDNA Synthesis Reaction Kit (Thermo Fisher) with an on-column DNase digestion according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Qiagen). ### Generation of sgZNF280A partial knockout cell lines

#### Construct preparation.

We modified the pCas9D10A–GFP plasmid (Addgene #44720) to create a single plasmid that expresses two single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) along with the Cas9D10A protein. To achieve this, we synthesized gene fragments containing both the human and mouse U6 promoters linked to two different sgRNAs (Supplementary Table 1), facilitated by Integrated DNA Technologies. Subsequently, we assembled these plasmid fragments with the gene fragments using the Gibson Assembly method (E2621L), following the manufacturer’s instructions.

sgRNAs targeting exon 2 of the human ZNF280A gene were designed using the CRISPR Design Tool (http://chopchop.cbu.uib.no). The following sequences were identified as sgRNAs: 5′-GATCTGATCTATGTTGGGG-3′ and 5′-TGCTGAAGTTCTCTTTGTC-3′. To minimize off-target effects, sgRNAs with high on-target scores and low off-target scores were selected.

#### Transfection.

For transfection, Lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen) was used according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Cells were cultured for 48 h after transfection to allow for genome editing. Transfected cells expressing GFP were sorted using fluorescence-activated cell sorting. Single-cell clones were expanded and screened for heterozygous knockout by T7 endonuclease assay followed by PCR amplicon sequencing in MGH CCIB DNA Core. Primers flanking the target exon were used to amplify genomic DNA extracted from clones.

#### T7E1 assay and sequencing.

Genomic DNA was extracted using the QIAamp DNA Micro Kit (#56304). The PCR amplification was performed with AmpliTaq Gold 360 Master Mix (#4398876) under specific cycling conditions: an initial denaturation at 95 °C for 10 min, followed by 40 cycles of denaturation at 95 °C for 30 s, annealing at 60 °C for 30 s and extension at 72 °C for 30 s, concluding with a final extension at 72 °C for 7 min. The following sequences were used to make amplicons: F-CAGAGAAACCGGCATGATGG and R-TGTCACATGGTTGCACTTAGG. After PCR, the amplicons underwent hybridization with a detailed temperature protocol: initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min, a gradient annealing from 95 °C down to 85 °C at a rate of −2 °C per second, and then from 85 °C down to 25 °C at −1 °C per second. After hybridization, T7 endonuclease I was added to each sample and incubated for 30 min at 37 °C. Finally, the samples were analysed on a 2% agarose gel. PCR products were sequenced by PCR amplicon sequencing in MGH CCIB DNA Core.

### cDNA rescue experiments in 22q11.2 patient-derived lymphocytes

A total of 2 × 106 immortalized patient-derived lymphocyte cells were washed three times in PBS and infected with 2 μg of pLX304-ZNF280A DNA using the mouse B cell nucleofector kit as per the manufacturer’s instructions (Lonza). Cells were recovered in antibiotic-free RPMI 1640 medium, supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% l-glutamine. Twenty-four hours after nucleofection, cells were spun onto poly-d-lysine-coated coverslips (50 μg ml−1) (Sigma-Aldrich) and IF was performed as described above. V5-positive cells were analysed, and the number of 53BP1 foci per cell was counted.

### Statistical analysis and reproducibility

Cell culture experiments were performed with at least three independent replicates (unless otherwise stated in the figure legends). The data are presented as mean ± s.d. or s.e.m. (as stated in the figure legends). Statistical significance (P values) was calculated using unpaired Student’s t-tests or log-rank test using GraphPad Prism version 7.0 through 10.0. Differences were considered statistically significant at a value of P < 0.05. Unless stated otherwise, *P < 0.05; **P < 0.005; ***P < 0.0005; ****P < 0.00005, as stated within the figure. No statistical method was used to predetermine the sample size. No data were excluded from the analyses. Data distribution was assumed to be normal, but this was not formally tested. Unless stated otherwise, the experiments were not randomized. Data collection and analysis were not performed blind to the conditions of the experiments.
